relationship: Guided stages use pV = 600 kPa·L with fixed particle count and speed. The experiment extends the same ideal-gas model to pV = 600 × (T/300) × relative gas amount, with particle speed proportional to sqrt(T).

learnerLoop.action: Compress and expand without a formula, collect three readings, inspect their products, predict a fresh pressure, then plan a target volume before testing.
learnerLoop.modelChange: Guided stages use pV = 600 kPa·L with fixed particle count and speed. The experiment extends the same ideal-gas model to pV = 600 × (T/300) × relative gas amount, with particle speed proportional to sqrt(T).
learnerLoop.evidence: Actual piston, impacts, gauge and recorded readings respond to the volume state. Products are disclosed after measurements, not before the initial observation.
learnerLoop.nextDecision: Revise a prediction, derive a new pressure or volume from the invariant, or collect another reading.

invariants: At a fixed temperature and gas amount: Pressure and volume satisfy the same constant product in the gauge, graph and calculation.
At a fixed temperature and gas amount: Constant temperature is represented by unchanged particle speed, not faster particles during compression.
At a fixed temperature and gas amount: Collision-frequency evidence changes with volume and stays distinct from particle-speed evidence.
Working assistance preserves the need to manipulate the piston and compare physical evidence.
safeAdaptations: Change target values, wording or working support within the supported volume range.
Add comparisons of pinned readings that test the inverse relationship.
In the final experiment, vary bath temperature and relative gas amount while preserving pV proportional to amount × absolute temperature.
nonGoals: Do not model non-ideal gas behaviour or transient heat exchange.
Do not replace the piston investigation with a formula-only quiz.

volume.domain: 2 to 8 L, in 0.05 L increments by pointer and 0.25 L by keyboard.
volume.output: Chamber size, gauge pressure and reading table.

pressure.description: Guided p = 600/V, including prediction at 4 L; experiment p = 600 × (T/300) × relative amount / V.
pressure.domain: 75 to 300 kPa guided; 18.75 to 1200 kPa in the expanded experiment.
pressure.source: Actual gas volume; predictions are entered separately in the working card.

product.domain: 600 kPa·L throughout the guided investigation; fixed for each chosen temperature and gas amount in the experiment.
product.output: Checks that predicted 2.5 L gives 240 kPa.

temperature.description: Absolute gas temperature T, instantaneously equilibrated with the bath.
temperature.domain: 300 K guided; 150 to 600 K in steps of 10 K in the experiment.

amount.description: Amount relative to the starting sample.
amount.domain: 1 guided; 0.5 to 2 in half-sample steps in the experiment.
amount.output: 9 to 36 representative particles and ideal-gas pressure.

modes.guided: Small ordered visual investigations, with model actions and in-place revision.
modes.experiment: Ungated temperature/amount/volume experiment with immutable records, frozen piston/curve comparisons, shared plot scaling and restored particle/condition snapshots.

dependencies: Compress 6 L to 3 L and return to 6 L. The gauge changes from 100 to 200 and back to 100 kPa; no formula card or numerical invariant is supplied.
Record three distinct volumes. A non-blocking nudge flags clustered readings; products and the curve are revealed after the third reading.
Predict 150 kPa for expansion from 3 L / 200 kPa to the unfamiliar 4 L. Explicit testing moves the piston; edits clear the verdict and restore the starting apparatus.
Supply the invariant 600 kPa·L and planned volume 2.5 L for a 240 kPa target. Method help is optional; the test animates actual volume, not the gauge prediction.
Ungated temperature/amount/volume experiment with immutable records, frozen piston/curve comparisons, shared plot scaling and restored particle/condition snapshots.
implementation.completion: New experiences require their model-derived criterion. Back and Forward revisit saved state without forcing a rerun; Repeat experience resets only that experience. Start over clears all session snapshots. Worked observations are not mastery claims.
limitations: This is the existing Physics/Chemistry cross-listed gas model, presented as a Chemistry prototype.
The starting sample uses eighteen representative particles; the displayed pressure follows the ideal-gas relationship, not measured 2D simulation impulses.

Temperature 300 K and gas amount remain fixed throughout the guided stages. The user-requested final extension varies both, with instantaneous bath equilibrium, no thermal transient, no non-ideal gas behaviour and no quantitative collision-pressure simulation.
Representative particle positions rescale with apparatus resizing; speed and scientific pressure remain model-derived, not collision-measured.
